causes.label: demand
causes.quote: demand reached 8,257 MW at the 6 pm dispatch interval. This is the highest winter demand on record exceeding the previous record of 8,197 MW set in 2008.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: The remaining 900 MW of capacity was on planned outages.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Almost 1,500 MW of this capacity was on unplanned outages that occurred at least 2 days prior, about half of which was the Callide C units that had yet to return to service from events on 25 May.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: The outage extension resulted in continued forced exports from Queensland into New South Wales for longer than forecast (Table 3). This contributed to both energy and FCAS high price outcomes.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding capacity to high prices and removing capacity contributed to the high prices.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: Co-optimisation between the Energy and FCAS markets.

causes.label: constraint_violation
causes.quote: As this constraint could not be satisfied it violated and when this occurs a violation penalty applies. In this case it was twice the price cap ($15,100/MWh) and contributed to setting the price in energy and FCAS.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: There was limited access to low-priced capacity from New South Wales. Upgrades to the Queensland-New South Wales interconnector (QNI) required Queensland to provide its own FCAS and forced exports from Queensland into New South Wales.

constraints_named.quote: AEMO invoked a financial constraint used to limit the accrual of negative residues from Queensland to New South Wales from 5.45 pm through to 9.30 pm.

interconnectors_named.name: QNI
interconnectors_named.quote: Upgrades to the Queensland-New South Wales interconnector (QNI) required Queensland to provide its own FCAS and forced exports from Queensland into New South Wales.

interconnectors_named.name: Terranora
interconnectors_named.quote: The constraints to manage the line outage forced exports out of Queensland into New South Wales across both the QNI and Terranora interconnectors

intervals.quote: The spot price in Queensland reached $5,434/MWh and $6,564/MWh for the 6 pm and 6.30 pm trading intervals respectively.

network_outages.quote: The outage extension resulted in continued forced exports from Queensland into New South Wales for longer than forecast (Table 3). This contributed to both energy and FCAS high price outcomes.

peak_price.quote: The spot price in Queensland reached $5,434/MWh and $6,564/MWh for the 6 pm and 6.30 pm trading intervals respectively.
